Re-derived the PRECISE root cause by reading tools/environments/wall_patterns.go source directly: linesIntersect's denom formula is (p1.X-p2.X)*(p3.Y-p4.Y) - (p1.Y-p2.Y)*(p3.X-p4.X); generateRandomWall (same file) draws every candidate wall axis-aligned (50/50 horizontal/vertical), and every RequiredPaths entry this repo declares is horizontal (shared doorRow Y) -- so whenever a candidate wall is ALSO horizontal, both (p1.Y-p2.Y) and (p3.Y-p4.Y) are exactly 0, making denom identically 0 REGARDLESS of either line's Y position, so linesIntersect returns false (no intersection) unconditionally for a horizontal wall vs a horizontal path -- including the case where the wall's Y exactly equals the path's Y with overlapping X ranges (a genuine collinear overlap that should be rejected but isn't). design_decision.ownership: Generic, content-agnostic obstacle-placement mechanism (ObstacleSpec, DungeonRegionParams.Obstacles, placeRegionObstacles) lives in encounter/dungeon.go alongside InitDungeon -- it never references crypt/coffin/altar/etc, mirroring the file's existing Theme-is-opaque discipline. Crypt-specific content (the approved Ref strings + which specs go in entrance/corridor/boss + the concrete CryptDungeonParams constructor) lives in a NEW file, encounter/crypt_dungeon.go, in the SAME module -- justified because ADR-0034 already classifies the `encounter` module as the (migration-pending) dnd5e rulebook loop, encounter/go.mod already depends on rulebooks/dnd5e by pseudo-version, and the repo's own test fixtures (dungeon_test.go's threeRegionDungeonParams / dungeonThemeCrypt) already treat 'the first crypt template's shape as encounter-owned content. Adding a NEW cross-module dependency from rulebooks/dnd5e -> encounter (which does not exist today) to host this instead would require publishing+tagging encounter and bumping rulebooks/dnd5e's go.mod for zero architectural benefit, since encounter already has the coupling in the other direction and no host (rpg-api) wiring exists yet either way (out of scope per #692).
design_decision.reserved_row_invariant: Placement candidates for EVERY region exclude the full doorRow row (all local x in [0,width)), not just the pre-existing required-path segment -- this single, simple, generic rule provably satisfies both 'required path stays clear' (a subset of the row) and the boss archetype's 'primary playable axis (>6 hex steps) stays clear' (the row spans the region's FULL width, always > the size-invariant floor validateDungeonParams already enforces at construction time). NOTE (session 004): this reservation is only load-bearing for OBSTACLE placement (placeRegionObstacles never chooses a doorRow candidate). It was NOT sufficient for GENERATED WALLS -- see boss_primary_axis_fix below for why walls needed a separate, two-layer fix.
design_decision.boss_primary_axis_fix: Session 004: independent seed sampling found generated walls (from tools/environments' PatternRandom, a separate module) could land on a boss region's doorRow beyond the pre-#819 required path's center-only endpoint. Root cause: tools/environments' path-safety validator operates on RAW continuous-position wall segments, checked against the required-path LINE, before this package's own hex-cell rounding -- a wall just off that line in continuous space can still round onto the doorRow cell. Fix is two layers, both inside the encounter module (tools/environments verified read-only, not modified, per module-isolation rules): (1) the required-path declaration itself now extends to the region's far edge for any ArchetypeBoss region regardless of chain position (previously only entrance/interior regions got full-width paths; boss-as-terminal got center-only, same as any other terminal archetype) -- necessary for stating intent to the upstream validator, but proven (via mutation) NOT sufficient alone; (2) stripReservedAxisWalls, a discrete, by-construction, boss-only post-rounding filter that unconditionally removes any wall landing on the full doorRow -- this is the actual load-bearing guarantee, verified by mutation (removing it while keeping the required-path extension still fails all 3 boss-axis tests against the same pinned failing-seed table). Non-boss terminal regions (chamber, etc.) are provably unaffected -- same literal code path as before #819, gated by an archetype check that's false for every existing fixture; full pre-existing suite (TwoChamberSuite, DungeonSuite, DungeonCompletionSuite, LockedBossDoorSuite) passes unchanged.
design_decision.altar_blocking_fix: Session 004: verified shipped asset contract measures altar at 2.057m, role 'obstacle' -- BlocksLoS=true, correcting this file's earlier unverified 'low vs tall' design guess (which had grouped altar with coffin as LoS-permissive). Coffin/tomb remains the ONLY approved piece with BlocksLoS=false per the verified contract.
design_decision.exact_statue_refs_fix: Session 004: verified no generic 'dnd5e:obstacles:statue' (or 'dnd5e:props:statue') key exists in the shipped asset contract. Replaced with the two promoted exact variants: CryptObstacleRefStatueReaper ('dnd5e:obstacles:statue-reaper') and CryptObstacleRefStatueKnightHooded ('dnd5e:obstacles:statue-knight-hooded'), both role obstacle/BlocksLoS=true. The first-crypt default places exactly one of each (a fixed pairing for visual variety, per instructions) -- no random-variant selection policy implemented, none needed. Coffin intentionally stays coffin-only; no tomb/sarcophagus variant added. Multi-hex visual footprints (a full sarcophagus or altar spanning more than one hex visually) remain an ACKNOWLEDGED #818 v1 limitation -- ObstacleData is single-anchor (one hex per instance); rpg-dnd5e-web#577 owns rendering/composition verification for how a client visually reconciles a single-hex anchor with a multi-hex asset mesh. Not addressed here -- out of scope for #819's toolkit-side placement logic.
design_decision.stale_comment_fix: Session 004: the task named 'space.go' but the actual stale text was in data.go's SpaceData.Obstacles field doc ('placement policy ... is out of scope for #818 -- see the crypt-placement issue that depends on it') -- #819 (this PR) IS that crypt-placement issue, now implemented, so the comment was corrected in place (data.go, not space.go) to point at DungeonRegionParams.Obstacles/placeRegionObstacles/CryptDungeonParams instead of a still-pending future issue. Doc-only; no logic touched.
design_decision.canonical_ref_namespace_fix: Session 005: verified finding -- the shipped asset manifest's actual keys use module 'dnd5e', type 'props' (e.g. 'dnd5e:props:coffin'), not the invented 'dnd5e:obstacles:<id>' namespace this file used through session 004. Corrected all six CryptObstacleRef* constants to the 'dnd5e:props:' prefix. Added a literal-value pinning test (TestCryptObstacleRefs_MatchCanonicalAssetManifestKeysExactly) since a shape-only regex test cannot catch a wrong TYPE segment drifting silently. Persisted-value contract: ObstacleData.Ref stores the FULL exact canonical 'module:type:id' string; a future #692 API projection may reuse an existing splitRef-style helper to decompose it for the wire, and rpg-dnd5e-web#577 (client rendering) only needs the tail id to resolve a mesh -- but the value THIS toolkit persists must match the asset manifest exactly, never a truncated or reconstructed form.
design_decision.upstream_generator_defect: Session 005: precisely re-derived (by reading tools/environments/wall_patterns.go source) the root cause behind the boss-primary-axis finding session 004 fixed with a downstream discrete workaround. linesIntersect's parallel denominator (p1.X-p2.X)*(p3.Y-p4.Y) - (p1.Y-p2.Y)*(p3.X-p4.X) is IDENTICALLY ZERO whenever both compared lines are horizontal (as every RequiredPaths entry in this repo's generators is, and as ~50% of generateRandomWall's candidate walls are) -- regardless of either line's actual Y position -- so it can never detect a horizontal wall collinear with and overlapping a horizontal required path. This is a DISTINCT defect from #758 (continuous/discrete rounding gap: a perfectly hex-snapped wall still triggers this bug) and #822 (tools/spatial LoS-grid-parity, different subsystem entirely). Filed upstream as rpg-toolkit#827 (tools/environments ownership, board 19 Feature='The Dungeon' Team='Platform' Status='Todo') rather than fixed in this PR -- #826 retains stripReservedAxisWalls as encounter's own deterministic interim guarantee; the generic source-level fix (a collinear-overlap branch in linesIntersect) belongs in tools/environments, a separate module this PR does not and should not modify.
design_decision.space_go_stale_comment_fix: Session 005: the ACTUAL stale comment the reviewer flagged (distinct from session 004's data.go fix) is in space.go's rebuildRoomFromData, the obstacle-occupancy-collision comment -- it claimed obstacles are 'host-authored (via AddObstacle), not generator output', which became false the moment #819's InitDungeon/placeRegionObstacles started generating obstacles too. Corrected the wording to cover both origins while keeping the substantive invariant intact (ANY collision is a genuine data error, because both AddObstacle and placeRegionObstacles only ever place at a cell already confirmed wall-free -- never a rounding artifact, regardless of origin).
